rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 59 makes explicit the warning implicit in verse 58.
rows.anchor: This verse clearly expresses the hidden warning that was concealed in the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who insist on believing only after the threatened punishment are told that the Prophet too must await it; judgment hinges on that punishment.
rows.anchor: On this punishment hinges the judgement. Readers may take a look at the explanation of verse 10.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the last Makkan sūrah in the group; three Madinan sūrahs follow to fulfil promises and threats made in the preceding Makkan sūrahs.
rows.anchor: This is the last Makkan sūrah of this group. After it come three Mad īnan sūrahs which mention the fulfillment of the promises and the materialization of threats

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aḥqāf shares its Qur’anic name with the previous sūrah and repeats that sūrah’s opening verses exactly.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ ānic name of this sūrah is the same as that of the previous one and its opening verses are exactly the same as well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment is certain, and polytheism and intercession provide no rational or revealed basis for ignoring its warning.
rows.anchor: there is nothing in reason and revelation to support such superstitions.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s message was foretold by a great Israelite witness, with its predictions also found in the Torah.
rows.anchor: by a great witness belonging to the Israelites and something whose predictions are mentioned in the Torah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents should not be misled by Jewish and Christian support, since those communities deny their own messengers and scriptures.
rows.anchor: these people are denying their own messengers and scriptures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should focus on communicating the Book; sincere, upright people conscious of their fate will believe, while the indifferent should not be expected to do so.
rows.anchor: His responsibility is of only communicating this Book to others

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of jinn who happened to hear the Qur’an became ardent admirers, showing that its lack of effect on the opponents reflects their hearts, not a defect in the Book.
rows.anchor: when a group of jinn who while passing by had a chance to listen to it, it became its ardent admirers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should continue patiently and leave the opponents to the fate they will soon meet.
rows.anchor: he should continue patiently with his work and consign them to their fate which they will encounter very soon.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is revealed by the mighty, wise God, yet those denying the Hereafter evade it.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ ān is a scripture revealed by God, the mighty and wise but those have denied the Hereafter are evading it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world was created with purpose rather than for amusement, so it must end and its intended outcome become manifest.
rows.anchor: This world is not meant for the entertainment of a merry-maker; however, the Almighty has created it with a great purpose and meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents trust deities and intercessors to save them at Judgment, although neither reason nor revelation supports that confidence.
rows.anchor: These people trust their deities and intercessors; they reckon that if ever the Day of Judgement comes, they will save them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The peoples of Noah, al-Rass, Thamūd, ‘Ād, Pharaoh, Lot, al-Aykah, and Tubb‘a denied messengers and were punished; the passage challenges the deniers’ doubt about a second creation.
rows.anchor: All of them denied the messengers. So, Our punishment descended upon them. Were We not able to create the first time?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah name Qāf is a sentence with its inchoative suppressed; unfolding it gives ‘This is Sūrah Qāf.’
rows.anchor: The inchoative ( mubtadā’) here is also suppressed, as has been indicated at many instances in this exegesis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majīd means glorious and exalted, and the Qur’an uses it as an attribute of both God and the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: It has been used in the Qur’ ān as an attribute both for God and for the Qur’ ān itself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every discourse reflects its author; God’s glory is reflected in His word and is evident throughout the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Every discourse is a reflection of its author. Just as God is glorious and exalted, His word is also glorious and exalted

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A receptive person cannot hear or read the Qur’an without awe; failure to respond signals a heart unable to savour truth.
rows.anchor: not impressed and over-awed by its glory and majesty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s grandeur is so powerful that it would shatter mountains if revealed to them, as the Qur’an itself says.
rows.anchor: This discourse would have shattered the mountains to pieces had it been revealed to them, let alone human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oath is by the exalted Book; Qur’anic oaths bear witness to the claim they support.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has sworn by this exalted Book. I have been explaining at various places of this exegesis that all such oaths signify bearing witness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s complement may be omitted when context makes it clear; Sūrah Ṣu‘ād 37:1–3 gives an especially clear example.
rows.anchor: A very clear example of such a suppression exists in S ūah Ṣu‘ād: 37:1-3.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s majesty refutes charges of poetry, magic, soothsaying, or satanic inspiration: its source is God, conveyed through Gabriel from the Guarded Tablet.
rows.anchor: By presenting the majesty of the Qur’ ān as evidence, these people are warned that it does not belong to these genres

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Burūj likewise calls it an exalted Qur’an whose origin is in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: In fact, this is an exalted Qur’ ān and its origin is in the preserved tablet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Takwīr calls the revelation a noble messenger’s word, rejects the charge that Muḥammad is possessed or that the Qur’an is a devil’s utterance, and calls it a reminder.
rows.anchor: This is the word brought by a noble messenger. He is endued with great power and held in honour before the Lord of the Throne.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s immunity from falsehood and the statement that only the purified touch it both point to its exaltedness.
rows.anchor: falsehood cannot reach it from in front of it nor from behind

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing argument of Sūrah al-Shu‘arā’ rejects the claim of satanic origin: devils neither brought the Qur’an down nor have the capacity or standing to do so.
rows.anchor: it was not the devils who brought this down; neither are they worthy of it nor is it in their power

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s miraculous eloquence and wisdom refute claims that it is not revelation; it is from the mighty, wise God and is unique and unparalleled.
rows.anchor: It has been revealed by the Almighty Who is mighty and wise. It is not an ordinary discourse; it is unique and unparalleled.

rows.speaker: these disbelievers
rows.claim: They found it strange that a warner from among themselves had come and said resurrection after death and becoming dust was very improbable.
rows.anchor: these disbelievers had said: “It is a very strange thing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle bal introduces an unveiling of the real motive behind their stated objection, which is only an excuse for evading reality.
rows.anchor: If the insinuations of this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their underlying resistance is that a person from their own community warns them of resurrection; accepting him as God’s messenger weighs heavily on them, so they call the return improbable.
rows.anchor: the real reason for their evasion is not what they are expressing but it is that they are surprised at the fact that a person from amongst themselves is warning them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance is the true cause: unwilling to accept one of their own as God’s messenger, they reject the Qur’an and deem the Hereafter unlikely; without arrogance they could recognize revelation and its arguments.
rows.anchor: the real reason of their evasion is their arrogance: they are not ready to accept someone among them as a messenger of God

rows.speaker: these people
rows.claim: They doubted the need for any messenger and, if one were sent, expected an angel or a leader from Mecca or Ṭā’if rather than a pauper.
rows.anchor: they reckoned that if the Almighty intended to send a messenger He would have chosen an angel for this purpose

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These objections were answered in earlier sūrahs, especially group four beginning with al-Furqān, whose central theme is establishing Muḥammad’s prophethood.
rows.anchor: in particular sūrahs of group 4 which begin with S ūrah al-Furqān. The comprehensive central theme of that group is to affirm the prophethood of Muḥ ammad (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this group’s context, the discourse addresses objections about death and resurrection that opponents use as excuses to oppose the Prophet.
rows.anchor: those objections are dealt with which they would raise on death and on the possibility of resurrection.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They regard resurrection as improbable because they think decomposed body parts cannot be assembled again.
rows.anchor: it is impossible for body parts to be put together once they decay and decompose within the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mistake is to analogize God’s knowledge to human knowledge, although God’s knowledge encompasses everything.
rows.anchor: they analogously regard the knowledge of God to be like their own whereas the knowledge of God is all-embracing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every body component consumed by the earth, since nothing is hidden from the Creator; He can restore the parts and form bodies as easily as He created everything from nothing.
rows.anchor: nothing is hidden from Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Besides His own knowledge, God preserves a register recording where people are buried, their body parts, and all their deeds and words, answering doubts about resurrection and accountability.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has preserved the record of all the words and deeds of humankind in a register.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While preserving this record could amaze the Arabs of the Prophet’s time, modern doubters who persist despite scientific advances are stubborn; they will believe only when accounts are handed over, too late to benefit.
rows.anchor: their accounts are handed over to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq denotes the Hereafter in verses 19 and 42, but here it means the Qur’an, which informs people about the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: as used in verses 19 and 42 of this sūrah signifies the Hereafter; however, it is evident from the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny the clear truth after its arrival, using earlier doubts to make the Hereafter seem improbable and presenting those doubts as cogent reasons, though their denial is blatant contradiction.
rows.anchor: they have denied an obvious reality and that too when it came to them with full clarity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘when it came to them’ means the Hereafter was already incontestable; ignorance of God’s books might once have been an excuse, but the Qur’an’s arrival removes it.
rows.anchor: the Hereafter which the Qur’ān is informing people of was an incontestable reality even earlier
